title: Pictures 1980–2002

description.main: Survey of Jeff Koons's paintings from 1980 to 2002, edited by Thomas Kellein for the Kunsthalle Bielefeld exhibition, with a long interview with the artist.
description.extended:
A survey of Jeff Koons's paintings from 1980 to 2002, made for his exhibition at the Kunsthalle Bielefeld and built around a long interview in which the artist tells his own story.

The catalogue accompanied Jeff Koons: Pictures 1980–2002 at the Kunsthalle Bielefeld (September 22 to November 10, 2002). Thomas Kellein, the Kunsthalle's director, edited it. It concentrates on the paintings but takes in the early sculptures too, which Koons calls "three-dimensional paintings." The plates run in order through each of his main painting series, and the book closes with an extended biography and bibliography. In Kellein's interview Koons recalls childhood drawing lessons, selling his first pictures at 11 in his father's decorating showroom, art school, meeting Ilona Staller while making the Made in Heaven series, and how his son's birth led to Celebration.

Koons (b. 1955) came up in New York in the early 1980s with The New, vacuum cleaners sealed in Plexiglas vitrines, and Equilibrium, basketballs floating in tanks of water. Later series include Banality, with the porcelain Michael Jackson and Bubbles (1988), and the flowering topiary Puppy (1992).

notes: Provenance: from the library of Agnes Gund, with her library stamp on an inside page. Catalogue of the exhibition at Kunsthalle Bielefeld, September 22 to November 10, 2002. Includes text by the artist. Page count: the Getty Research Institute record gives 112 pp.; D.A.P. lists 120 pp. Out of print.
